slides.say: Given: x is equal to fourteen a plus six, a is a positive integer, and x is divisible by ten. Which of the following could be the value of a?
Divisible by ten, so it's all about the last digit. [short pause] We'll solve it two ways, working out which last digit a needs, and then testing the choices.

[short pause] Let's start with the last digit. Remember the sign for ten, the last digit is zero. So fourteen a plus six ends in zero. And what plus six ends in zero? Something that ends in four. So fourteen a ends in four.
at: fourteen a plus six ends in zero

slides.say: And remember, the last digit of a product comes only from the last digits. So four times the last digit of a has to end in four. Four times one is four, and four times six is twenty-four. No other digit works.
So a ends in one or six. Only three hundred forty-six ends in six, so choice number four is our answer.
at: a ends in one or six
choice number four is our answer

slides.say: [pause] Another way is to test the choices, with last digits only. Three forty-three. Four times three is twelve, it ends in two, and two plus six is eight. x would end in eight, so it's out.

Three forty-four. Four times four is sixteen, it ends in six, and six plus six is twelve, so x ends in two. Out. Three forty-five. Four times five is twenty, it ends in zero, and zero plus six is six. Out.
Three choices are out, so three forty-six, choice number four. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next question.
